overview: Letters (1936): broadcasters ask State about Dairen's Oriental Radio Association, which solicited QRA cards; State finds no information, suggesting it's an amateur group.

people.name: James W. Baldwin
people.role: Managing Director, National Association of Broadcasters

people.name: Kenneth Warner
people.role: Official associated with the American Radio Relay League

subfiles.title: Baldwin asks Moore about the Oriental Radio Association
subfiles.from: James W. Baldwin, Managing Director, National Association of Broadcasters
subfiles.to: R. Walton Moore, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Baldwin requests information about the Oriental Radio Association in connection with an enclosed letter sent to a member broadcasting station.
subfiles.summary: Baldwin asks Moore whether State knows anything about Dairen's Oriental Radio Association.

subfiles.title: Oriental Radio Association solicitation for QRA cards
subfiles.about: The Oriental Radio Association requests QRA cards for an exhibition planned alongside its winter general meeting in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Dairen's Oriental Radio Association asks a broadcaster for QRA cards for its winter meeting exhibition.

subfiles.title: State Department reply concerning the Oriental Radio Association
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, Assistant Secretary of State, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: James W. Baldwin, Managing Director, National Association of Broadcasters
subfiles.about: The Department reports that official inquiries produced no information about the Oriental Radio Association and suggests consulting the American Radio Relay League.
subfiles.summary: State finds no information on Dairen's Oriental Radio Association, suggesting Baldwin contact the American Radio Relay League.

interest: Shows a 1936 US inquiry into the obscure Oriental Radio Association in Dairen, Manchuria.
